inline:Corrective Divergence is logically incompatible with the countercondition of a checklist so unambiguous that disagreement is impossible: a checklist that is unambiguous to all competent readers cannot yield the initial disagreement the target requires, so the target's own marker excludes the very case it must cover.
The problem asks for evidence within a single evaluation that distinguishes genuine reliability gain from mere compliance. The target defines Corrective Divergence: initial internal disagreement on checklist items that converges to the correct answer. In the unambiguous-checklist countercondition, every competent reader reaches the same reading; there is no initial disagreement to record. A single evaluation is statically one run, so the observation token cannot produce divergence that the deterministic checklist precludes.
